## 8. Assistant (2026-11-15T14:39:53.585Z)

Matt’s GitHub account is `mvuk`. The useful baselines are his Bark/CDK payment processor and Bark-backed paid relay writes; his Blossom repository contains protocol specifications. I’ll build a proof-gated payment desk with payment reuse checks, Ark refresh/exit planning, and receipts that distinguish verified proofs from pending settlement. [Bark processor](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk-payment-processors/tree/main/crates/bark), [paid writes](https://github.com/mvuk/strfry-bark-paid-writes)

The apparent event is Nut November, which runs through November 27, 2026. [Event site](https://nutnovember.org/)

---

## 9. Assistant (2026-11-15T14:44:08.861Z)

The payment checks and SQLite ledger are in place. They bind each accepted payment to an immutable recipient and intent, reject reuse, and prepare a settlement request without marking it paid. I’ve also added the native verifier adapter and read-only Cashu/Bark clients; I’m now building the demo and testing rejection paths.

---

## 10. Assistant (2026-11-15T14:53:17.076Z)

I found the existing native verifier and mainnet proof in WSL. I’ll test the adapter against that proof and then against a corrupted copy. The demo stays in a separate namespace so fixture results cannot authorize a connected payment.

---

---

## 16. Assistant (2026-11-15T15:11:58.569Z)

The previous turn produced a committed prototype and verified the real M16 proof path. I’ll now work on the missing payment integration: binding proof admission to actual Cashu quotes and Bark wallet operations, with recovery after retries or crashes.

## 17. Assistant (2026-11-15T15:17:04.782Z)

The published Cashu SDK supports preparing blinded outputs before submission, which gives us a way to persist them for recovery. I’m building the bridge around that: the proof desk will handle blinded messages, while the wallet retains the bearer secrets. I’m also setting up an isolated test mint to verify actual signatures and recovery.

---

## 18. Assistant (2026-11-15T15:34:15.098Z)

The isolated Bitcoin Core node is running, and the issuance bridge now binds a mint quote, receiving script, amount, and wallet key before admitting a payment. I’m testing the recovery path where the mint issues signatures but its reply is lost; the wallet should recover those same outputs without requesting another issuance.

---

## 19. Assistant (2026-11-15T15:43:34.295Z)

The bridge now passes 53 automated tests. They cover quote substitution, overissuance, reorg checks, fixture/live isolation, and recovery from a lost issuance reply. The test mint has not connected to its Core backend yet; I’m checking the running container and stored RPC settings before retrying it.

---

## 20. Assistant (2026-11-15T16:00:23.188Z)

The first end-to-end run reached a real CDK deposit with two confirmations. It then stopped at signature authorization, before any issuance. I’m checking the SDK’s prepared request against its public verifier; the bridge is correctly refusing the request while those checks disagree.

---

## 21. Assistant (2026-11-15T16:06:24.250Z)

The mint issued test ecash, and a restarted wallet recovered the same outputs after the dropped reply. DLEQ signature verification and the unspent checks passed. The final token audit hit a separate SDK requirement: decoding needs the loaded mint keysets. I’m fixing that call and rerunning the full test.

---

## 22. Assistant (2026-11-15T16:19:50.965Z)

The complete deposit-to-ecash recovery test passed: 25,000 regtest sats produced six verified proofs, with one issuance request and one restoration request after the lost reply. I’m finishing owner-signed quote registration, connected desktop/phone checks, and a reproducible launcher that cleans up only its own test stack.

---

## 23. Assistant (2026-11-15T16:36:17.706Z)

Both the fixture and connected desktop/phone checks passed. I also separated the mint’s payment deadline from proof admission, so an eligible deposit can be proved later without stranding it while the proof is generated. I’m committing this milestone; actual Bark execution and rollover management remain next.

Bark 0.8.1 supports delegated refresh, so the wallet can sign ahead of time and let the server include it in a later round. Its API has no fee-cap parameter; I’m checking the fee calculation and request validation before enabling that action.

The isolated Ark server is starting on a fresh regtest chain. I’ll test delegated refresh and recoverable exit data there. Production spending will remain disabled until the wallet can enforce a fee limit when it signs.

## 30. Assistant (2026-11-15T16:57:12.337Z)

The refresh request is now persisted before Bark receives it. If the reply is lost, the desk checks wallet rounds and history instead of resending. It will report completion only after finding the successor VTXOs, checking the value and fee, and confirming their anchors with Core.

---

The desk can now inspect Bark VTXOs and offer delegated refresh for regtest. The new recovery tests cover lost replies, restarts, changed requests or wallets, fee discrepancies, and reorgs.
